note: Expected values are exact (fractions or decimals) and were derived by hand from the cited definitions, then checked against TA-Lib. Each case's derivation is written out so it can be repeated with a calculator. Cases marked definition_boundary need no source: the value follows from the definition alone.
published_numeric_examples: None. The StockCharts ChartSchool worked examples are downloadable spreadsheets (cs-rsi.xls, cs-adx.xls, cs-atr.xls, cs-bbands.xls and similar). They were not downloaded in this task, so no published numeric example could be sourced.

source.definition: Arithmetic mean of the last N closes; see https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-overlays/moving-averages-simple-and-exponential

EMA with k=2/(N+1) started from the plain mean of the first N closes; see https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-overlays/moving-averages-simple-and-exponential
source.derivation: k=2/(3+1)=1/2. The first value (index 2) is the plain mean of the first 3 closes, (11+12+13)/3=12. Then value = 1/2 x close + 1/2 x previous: 11 gives 23/2, 14 gives 51/4, 15 gives 111/8, 13 gives 215/16, 12 gives 407/32, 15 gives 887/64.

source.definition: Linearly weighted mean, newest close weighted N and oldest 1, divided by N(N+1)/2 (TA-Lib function list)
P. Mulloy, Technical Analysis of Stocks & Commodities, January 1994: 2*EMA - EMA(EMA)
source.derivation: EMA1 (k=1/2) is 12, 23/2, 51/4, 111/8, 215/16, 407/32, 887/64 from index 2. EMA2 is the EMA of EMA1, started at index 4 from the mean of the first 3 EMA1 values, (12+23/2+51/4)/3=145/12, then 1/2 x EMA1 + 1/2 x previous EMA2. DEMA = 2 x EMA1 - EMA2; at index 4 that is 2x51/4 - 145/12 = 161/12.

source.definition: J. Bollinger, Bollinger on Bollinger Bands (2001); https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-overlays/bollinger-bands
source.derivation: Middle = mean of the last 3 closes. The spread is the population standard deviation of those 3 closes; for 11,12,13 it is sqrt(2/3)=0.816496580928. Upper = 12 + 2 x 0.816496580928 = 13.632993161855, lower = 12 - 1 x 0.816496580928 = 11.183503419072 (nbdevup=2, nbdevdn=1). Irrational values are written to 12 decimals.

source.definition: J. Welles Wilder Jr., New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems (1978); https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-overlays/parabolic-sar
source.derivation: Step 0.02, maximum 0.2. Wilder's rule: next SAR = SAR + AF x (EP - SAR), AF grows by the step each time a new extreme point (EP) is made, up to the maximum. TA-Lib starts long: SAR(1)=low(0)=18, EP=high(1)=22, AF=0.02. SAR(2)=18+0.02x4=18.08; high(2)=24 is a new EP so AF=0.04: SAR(3)=18.08+0.04x(24-18.08)=18.3168; EP 26, AF 0.06: SAR(4)=18.777792; EP 28, AF 0.08: SAR(5)=19.51556864 (low 22 stays above it, no reversal). SAR(6) would be 20.1944 but low(6)=20 is below it, so the trend reverses: SAR(6)=EP=28, new EP=20, AF back to 0.02. Then SAR(7)=28+0.02x(20-28)=27.84, EP 19, AF 0.04: SAR(8)=27.4864, EP 18, AF 0.06: SAR(9)=26.917216. SAR(10) would be 26.3822 but high(10)=27 is above it, so the trend reverses again: SAR(10)=EP=18. Wilder's optional cap by the prior two lows or highs never binds from the third value on; TA-Lib does not apply it at the first step (observed).
source.convention: TA-Lib start (long, SAR=first low) and no cap at the first step (observed)

source.definition: Midpoint of the highest high and lowest low over N bars (TA-Lib function list)
source.derivation: Over the latest 3 bars: (highest high + lowest low)/2. Index 2: highs 12,13,14 and lows 10,11,11 give (14+10)/2=12; index 3: highs 13,14,13 and lows 11,11,9 give (14+9)/2=23/2.

source.definition: Maximum of the last N highs (TA-Lib MAX applied to the high column)
source.derivation: Highest of the latest 3 highs: indices 0-2 are 12,13,14 so 14; indices 1-3 are 13,14,13 so 14; indices 2-4 are 14,13,15 so 15.

source.definition: Minimum of the last N lows (TA-Lib MIN applied to the low column)
source.derivation: Lowest of the latest 3 lows: indices 0-2 are 10,11,11 so 10; indices 1-3 are 11,11,9 so 9; indices 2-4 are 11,9,12 so 9.

source.definition: J. Welles Wilder Jr., New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems (1978); https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/relative-strength-index-rsi (first averages are simple, later averages are (previous x (N-1) + current) / N)
source.derivation: Changes: +1, +1, -2, +3, +1, -2, -1, +3. First averages are simple means of the first 3 changes: gain (1+1+0)/3=2/3, loss (0+0+2)/3=2/3, so RSI=100x(2/3)/(2/3+2/3)=50 at index 3. Next change +3: gain=(2/3x2+3)/3=13/9, loss=(2/3x2+0)/3=4/9, RSI=100x13/17=1300/17. Later values repeat the (previous x 2 + current)/3 smoothing.

source.definition: G. Appel (1979); https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/macd-moving-average-convergence-divergence-oscillator
source.derivation: TA-Lib convention. Slow EMA(3), k=1/2, starts at index 2 from the mean of closes 11,12,13 = 12. TA-Lib starts the fast EMA(2), k=2/3, at the same index from the mean of the two closes ending there, (12+13)/2=25/2, instead of running it from index 1. MACD(2)=25/2-12=1/2 (not yet output). Index 3: slow=1/2x11+1/2x12=23/2, fast=2/3x11+1/3x25/2=23/2, so MACD=0. The signal EMA(2), k=2/3, starts at index 3 from the mean of the first two MACD values, (1/2+0)/2=1/4; histogram =0-1/4=-1/4. Standalone EMAs (talipp, pandas-ta-classic) start the fast line earlier and give different early values; see docs/INDICATOR-MENU.md.
source.convention: TA-Lib seeding of the fast average (see derivation)

source.definition: G. Lane; https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/stochastic-oscillator-fast-slow-and-full
source.derivation: Raw %K = 100 x (close - lowest low of 3) / (highest high of 3 - lowest low of 3): index 2 is 100x(13-10)/(14-10)=75, index 3 is 100x(11-9)/(14-9)=40, index 4 is 100x(14-9)/(15-9)=250/3. Slow K = mean of 2 raw values: index 4 is (40+250/3)/2=185/3. Slow D = mean of 2 slow K values.

source.definition: D. Lambert, Commodities magazine (1980); https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/commodity-channel-index-cci
source.derivation: Typical price TP=(high+low+close)/3: 11, 12, 38/3. Mean of TP = 107/9. Mean absolute deviation = (8/9+1/9+7/9)/3=16/27. CCI = (TP - mean)/(0.015 x deviation) = (7/9)/(0.015x16/27) = 175/2 at index 2.

source.definition: G. Quong and A. Soudack (1989); https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/money-flow-index-mfi
source.derivation: TP=(high+low+close)/3 per bar: 11, 12, 38/3, 11, ... Money flow = TP x volume, positive when TP rose from the previous bar, negative when it fell. Index 3 uses bars 1-3: +12x120=1440, +38/3x90=1140, -11x150=1650. MFI=100x(1440+1140)/(1440+1140+1650)=8600/141.

source.definition: L. Williams; https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/williams-r
source.derivation: -100 x (highest high of 3 - close) / (highest high of 3 - lowest low of 3). Index 2: -100x(14-13)/(14-10)=-25; index 3: -100x(14-11)/(14-9)=-60.

source.definition: https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/rate-of-change-roc
Change of the close over N bars as a fraction of the earlier close, (close - close N bars earlier) / close N bars earlier (TA-Lib function list, ROCP); the same quantity as ROC divided by 100.

Change of the close over N bars as a fraction of the earlier close, (close - close N bars earlier) / close N bars earlier (TA-Lib function list, ROCP). One bar is the hourly return used by the hourly price features.
Close minus the close N bars earlier (TA-Lib function list)
source.derivation: Close minus the close 2 bars earlier: 13-11=2, 11-12=-1, 14-13=1, 15-11=4, ...

source.definition: J. Welles Wilder Jr., New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems (1978); https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/average-directional-index-adx
source.derivation: TA-Lib convention, N=2. Per bar: +DM = high rise if it beats the low fall and is positive; -DM the mirror; TR = max(high-low, |high-previous close|, |low-previous close|). TA-Lib seeds the smoothed sums with the first N-1 values (TR(1)=2, +DM(1)=1, -DM(1)=0) and applies S = S - S/N + x from index N, so index 2 has TR sum 2-1+3=4 and +DM sum 1-1/2+1=3/2: +DI=100x1.5/4=75/2, -DI=0, DX=100. Index 3: +DI=25/2, -DI=100/3, DX=500/11. The first ADX (index 2N-1=3) is the mean of the DX values at indices 2 and 3, (100+500/11)/2=800/11; later ADX=(previous x (N-1) + DX)/N. Wilder's textbook seed (sum of the first N values) gives different early numbers that converge; see docs/INDICATOR-MENU.md.
source.convention: TA-Lib seeding of the smoothed sums (see derivation)

source.definition: J. Welles Wilder Jr., New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems (1978); https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/average-directional-index-adx
source.derivation: Same smoothing as the ADX case. Index 2: 100 x (3/2) / 4 = 75/2; index 3: smoothed +DM 1/2... (3/2 - 3/4 + 0 = 3/4), smoothed TR 4 - 2 + 4 = 6, so 100 x (3/4) / 6 = 25/2.
source.convention: TA-Lib seeding of the smoothed sums (see derivation)

source.definition: J. Welles Wilder Jr., New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems (1978); https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/average-directional-index-adx
source.derivation: Same smoothing as the ADX case. -DM is 0 at indices 1 and 2, so -DI=0 at index 2; index 3: low falls 11 -> 9 so -DM=2 and the smoothed -DM is 0 - 0 + 2 = 2; smoothed TR is 6, so -DI=100x2/6=100/3.
source.convention: TA-Lib seeding of the smoothed sums (see derivation)

source.definition: T. Chande, Technical Analysis of Stocks & Commodities, September 1995; https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/aroon
source.derivation: Window of the latest 4 bars (N+1). Up = 100 x (3 - bars since the highest high) / 3; down uses the lowest low. Index 3: highs 12,13,14,13 peak at index 2 (1 bar ago) so up=200/3; lows 10,11,11,9 bottom at index 3 (0 bars ago) so down=100.

source.definition: J. Welles Wilder Jr., New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems (1978); https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/average-true-range-atr
source.derivation: TR(1)=max(2,|13-11|,|11-11|)=2, TR(2)=3, TR(3)=max(4,|13-13|,|9-13|)=4. First ATR (index 2) is the mean of the first 2 TR values, 5/2; then (previous x 1 + TR)/2: index 3 is (5/2+4)/2=13/4.

source.definition: Population standard deviation of the last N closes; https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/standard-deviation-volatility
source.derivation: Population standard deviation of the latest 3 closes (divide by 3, not 2). For 11,12,13: sqrt(((1)^2+0+(1)^2)/3)=sqrt(2/3)=0.816496580928; for 12,13,11 the same; for 13,11,14 the mean is 38/3 and the result is 1.247219128925.
